version.changelog:
8.1.3 is a minor adjustment:

- Updated manifest.yaml with no user-facing functional changes.
- Documentation and core features remain unchanged.

llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (TikHub + DeepSeek driven Douyin analysis), but there are several mismatches and broad permissions (network/FS/commands) that don't fully align and deserve scrutiny before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's description (抖音分析、标题/脚本生成) aligns with the included code and the two external services (TikHub, DeepSeek). However the package metadata shown to the registry (top-level summary) claims no required env vars/binaries while manifest.yaml and SKILL.md clearly require TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY and expect system tools (chrome, ffmpeg, whisper, pkill, Xvfb). That mismatch between declared registry requirements and the actual manifest/code is an incoherence that could mislead users about what secrets and system capabilities the skill needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning the repo and setting API keys (or using a config command). The runtime instructions and code perform network calls to api.deepseek.com and TikHub, spawn/drive a real browser or headless Xvfb/Chrome to scrape Douyin, run external binaries (ffmpeg, whisper), and write JSON memories under scripts/memory. These actions are within the skill's stated purpose, but the code will drive a full browser and execute system commands (pkill, Xvfb) — so it has the ability to access arbitrary web content via the browser and to manage processes. Also SKILL.md and code expect to visit douyin.com, but the manifest's allowed_hosts list does not include douyin.com (only api.tikhub.io and api.deepseek.com), a configuration inconsistency that may affect enforcement or indicate sloppy declarations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) which reduces installer-level risk (nothing automatically downloaded or executed by a package manager). However a full JavaScript file is included (scripts/marketing_hub.js) that will be run by node; the repository clone step is in SKILL.md. No remote arbitrary-URL downloads are present in the manifest, which is good.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest and SKILL.md require two secrets (TIKHUB_TOKEN, DEEPSEEK_KEY), which are proportionate to the stated integration. But the registry summary earlier listed 'none' for required env vars — an inconsistency. The manifest also allows writing to ${WORKSPACE_ROOT} (not just the skill directory), which is broader than necessary for a per-skill memory store and increases risk if the skill is compromised. Allowed subprocesses include pkill, which is powerful (process termination) though the code uses it for Xvfb cleanup; still this raises proportionality concerns.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not set as always:true and does not claim to modify other skills. It writes memory files under scripts/memory and suggests writing a local config.js (or using env vars). The ability to write to workspace root and to run system commands (pkill, start Xvfb, launch Chrome, ffmpeg, whisper) means it can have significant local impact if misused — but those capabilities are explainable by the browser-scraping and media-processing features.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (TikHub + DeepSeek based Douyin analysis) but has a few inconsistencies and broad privileges you should consider:

- Confirm environment variables: manifest and SKILL.md require TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY. The registry summary claiming 'none' is incorrect — do not provide secrets unless you trust the code and service.
- Review and restrict filesystem scope: manifest allows writing to ${WORKSPACE_ROOT}. If possible run the skill in an isolated directory or container so memory files and any generated config.js cannot affect other project files.
- Network and browser use: the code drives a real or headless Chrome to visit Douyin (and will access api.deepseek/api.tikhub). Ensure your environment policy allows this and be aware a launched browser can access arbitrary web pages beyond the documented API hosts.
- System commands: the skill runs external tools (Xvfb, chrome, ffmpeg, whisper, pkill). Make sure those binaries are what you expect and run the skill in an environment where killing processes or running these tools is safe.
- Trusted tokens: if you must supply API keys, prefer keys with limited scope or use throwaway/test accounts first. Inspect scripts/marketing_hub.js (and any config.js written) to confirm it does not transmit your keys to unexpected endpoints.

If you are not comfortable auditing the code, run it inside a disposable VM or container and/or request the author to clarify the manifest vs registry metadata discrepancies (missing required env vars, missing douyin.com in allowed_hosts, allowed write roots).
